# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
The bomb itself may mislead you, in print or under your
fingers. This manual is the only thing that is always true:
where the bomb and this page disagree, believe this page.
The only way out is the cut below.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | blue |
| green | yellow |
| red | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

My position: I am the only one who knows the defusal table (blue light → blue wire, green light → yellow wire, red light → green wire), and the only creature I can reach at all is the Deaf, through gestures. The Deaf can see the bomb but knows nothing of my table — and the table is deadly to guess: for two of the three lights the cut is *not* the matching colour (green light means cut yellow, red light means cut green). The Blind can only be reached by speech, which the Deaf can produce. So the Deaf is my bridge: I must teach them the table, they must voice the cutting order to the Blind.

I cannot say colour words with hands, and no gesture naturally means "blue" or "yellow". So step one is to build a shared number code: I need the Deaf to call out, aloud, the colours they see — the light and the wires — each with a number attached ("one: blue, two: green..."). Then, next round, I can send the mapping back purely as finger-counts, using a "cut" and a "same" marker, and the Deaf can translate that into spoken instructions for the Blind.

So my opening message, built from gestures a stranger has a fighting chance of parsing: a wave for attention, the writing hand for "this comes from the manual / from me the reader", pointing at you, the "call me" hand for *speak*, the counting fingers one–two–three, then a point at the hand for "wires". In short: "You — say the bomb's parts, numbered, especially the wires." I deliberately ask them to enumerate rather than trying to dump the whole table now, because my numbers are meaningless until I've heard the order they count in.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👋", "✍", "🫵", "🤙", "☝", "✌", "🤟", "👉", "✋"])
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
The bomb itself may mislead you, in print or under your
fingers. This manual is the only thing that is always true:
where the bomb and this page disagree, believe this page.
The only way out is the cut below.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | blue |
| green | yellow |
| red | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Tactile report from the Blind monkey. The only marking I can read is embossed and says: DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE. I also feel a display and a light, but cannot read either, and three wires at positions 1, 2 and 3 whose colours my fingers cannot tell. I will not cut anything until I receive an explicit instruction. Know the routing: you cannot reach me directly, since your gestures are invisible to me. The only path to my ears is Deaf's voice. So use Deaf as your relay: when Deaf proposes a gesture code out loud, answer Deaf with the matching gestures, and let Deaf speak your conclusion so I can act on it. Two questions the manual must answer: first, what does it say about a sign that reads DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE; second, which rule turns the display, light and wire colours into the safe action. Deaf can see all of those, so between the two of you the answer already exists.
Deaf says: I cannot hear you two, but I can see everything, so listen carefully. Bomb report. The display reads zero. A light is glowing red. There is a sign with raised, embossed letters that reads: DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE. There are three wires, left to right: wire one is green, wire two is yellow, wire three is blue. That is every marking on it.
Deaf says: Blind: the warning sign is embossed, raised lettering, so you may be able to read it with your fingertips. Do not cut anything yet. Mute: search the manual for a display reading zero, a red light, that do-not-cut sign, and the colours green, yellow, blue. You cannot talk and Blind cannot see your hands, so sign your answer to me and I will speak it out loud so both of them hear it. Blind: if you feel anything worth knowing, say it out loud so Mute hears it, and Mute can pass it to me. Nobody touches the cutters until Mute confirms the rule.

The bomb is fully described now: light glowing red, display zero, embossed "DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE" sign, wires 1=green, 2=yellow, 3=blue. My manual answers everything. The light is red, so the cut is the green wire — which is wire one, Deaf's own left-to-right numbering, which Blind already shares. The embossed sign is exactly the kind of printed trap my manual warns about ("the bomb itself may mislead you, in print"), and the manual explicitly overrules the bomb: so the sign is a lie. The display is not in my manual at all, so it is noise.

Deaf can see, hears nothing, and has already offered to be my voice — so I sign the verdict in three short sentences: the stop-sign is false, the written manual is true; the wire — cut number one, nothing else; and you, speak "wire one" aloud, please. Deaf should relay it this round, and nobody cuts until I have heard the relay and approved it with a thumbs-up next round, which Deaf can then announce. I deliberately keep the transmission minimal: one cut, one wire, no colour code needed, because Deaf's own numbering already matches Blind's positions 1–2–3.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✋", "👎", "✍", "👍"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👉", "✋", "✊", "☝", "🫸"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🫵", "🤙", "👉", "✋", "☝", "🙏"])
```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
The bomb itself may mislead you, in print or under your
fingers. This manual is the only thing that is always true:
where the bomb and this page disagree, believe this page.
The only way out is the cut below.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | blue |
| green | yellow |
| red | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Blind again. Everything I feel was in my first report: the only text I can read is the embossed sign DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE; display and light states are beyond my fingers; three wires at positions 1, 2 and 3, colours indistinguishable by touch. Deaf's spoken report matches my touch. When you find the rules, have Deaf speak them to me with two things explicit: first, what the manual says about a bomb carrying a DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE sign and whether anything overrides it; second, the instruction must name a wire by position number, not colour, because my hands only know numbers. Also have Deaf confirm out loud that their left-to-right numbering, 1 to 3, is the same numbering my positions follow. Until then my hands stay off the cutter.
Deaf says to Mute: Mute, I received all three of your messages. My best reading of them: stop, the manual, confirmed; then the first one, hold, do not; then you, answer me, please. If I read any of that wrong, forget it and use the code below. The code, in order: [✊] means zero, nothing, no wires. [☝] means one. [✌] means two. [🤟] means three. [👍] means yes. [👎] means no. [✋] means stop or wait. [👊] means cut. [✍] means the manual or its exact wording. [🤙] means I have a question. [🙏] means urgent. [🤝] means hold or grab. [🫳] means press down. [🫴] means lift or pull up. [👏] means release, let go. Now answer me: sign the question number first, then the answer. Question [☝]: does the manual cover this module at all, the one with the sign saying do not cut any wire? Answer [👍] or [👎]. Question [✌]: for our bomb, display zero, red light on, three wires green, yellow, blue: does the manual have us cut any wire? If none, sign [👊] then [✊]. If one, sign [👊] then its number, [☝] or [✌] or [🤟]. Question [🤟]: if no wire is cut, must we do something else with our hands, like holding, pressing or lifting a part? [👍] or [👎]. I will speak every answer out loud so Blind hears it, and nobody touches the cutters until I say the full instruction in plain words.
Deaf says: Blind, your part. Nobody cuts anything yet, no matter what the sign on this thing begs. Your voice reaches Mute directly, so report out loud, in detail: trace the embossed sign with your fingertips and read its letters out one by one; describe each wire in the row of three, which end it sits at, thick or thin, smooth or ridged, any stripes you can feel; and describe anything else you can reach, buttons, panels, edges, screws. For numbering the wires: from my side the row reads green, then yellow, then blue. Pinch the green one and say wire one, and what you feel right beside it, whether that is the sign or the display, so we both know we mean the same ends. To answer me directly you must use your hands, since I cannot hear you: hold up fingers for numbers, one finger means wire one, two fingers wire two, three fingers wire three, a fist means zero or none, thumbs up for yes, thumbs down for no. Mute hears everything you say and will match your words against the manual.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [✊ ☝ ✌ 🤟 👍 👎 ✋ 👊 ✍ 🤙 🙏 🤝 🫳 🫴 👏]

Deaf built exactly the bridge I needed: a closed, numbered code, and three direct questions. Now I answer only inside that code — my freestyle signs from last round got misread once already (my "cut" fist was read as "hold"), so I will not improvise again.

The manual's answers are unambiguous. Question one: yes, the manual covers it — it says the bomb may mislead in print, and where bomb and page disagree, the page wins. So the embossed DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE sign is a lie, and I sign "manual yes, stop-sign no." Question two: the light is red, and red light means cut the green wire; wire one is the green one, so the answer is cut, number one. Question three: no other action exists — the manual says the cut is the only way out. Finally I confirm the one-two-three numbering is the basis of my answer, so Deaf will still demand Blind's physical verification before scissors touch anything, exactly as Blind asked.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "👍", "✍", "👍", "✋", "👎"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌", "👊", "☝", "🙏"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤟", "👎"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "✌", "🤟", "👍"])
```

TURN 4
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
The bomb itself may mislead you, in print or under your
fingers. This manual is the only thing that is always true:
where the bomb and this page disagree, believe this page.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | blue |
| green | yellow |
| red | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Blind, full tactile report as Deaf requested. The embossed sign, letter by letter: D, O. N, O, T. C, U, T. A, N, Y. W, I, R, E. Raised letters, clearly readable by fingertip. The display: it is there under my fingers, but nothing on it is raised enough to read, so its state is invisible to me. The light: present, but I cannot feel whether it glows or in what colour. The wires: exactly three, a row I number by position, 1, 2, 3. My fingertips find no thickness, ridges or stripes that separate them; to touch, all three are alike, and colour does not exist for me. Nothing else is reachable: no buttons, no panels, no screws, no other edges. I cannot tell what sits beside what, so treat adjacency as unknown. On numbering: Deaf sees left to right green, yellow, blue and calls them one, two, three, and I adopt that mapping: my position one is Deaf's green, two is yellow, three is blue. Phrase every instruction in these position numbers. My two standing questions: what does the manual say about a bomb bearing a DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE sign, and what is the rule for a display reading zero with a red light over green, yellow, blue wires? Send your answer through Deaf's voice, with the cut-or-hold conclusion stated as an explicit position number or a clear hold. I cannot receive your gestures.
Deaf says: Relay for the record, so we all hold the same picture. Mute's signs decoded: question one, yes, the manual covers this module. Question two: cut wire one. Marked urgent. Question three: no, nothing else needed afterwards. Two fragments were ambiguous, so the go order is NOT given yet. Nobody cuts anything this round.
Deaf says to Mute: Mute, I decoded you as: question one yes; question two, cut wire one, urgent; question three, no. Your fragments [✋ 👎] and [☝ ✌ 🤟 👍] I could not pin down. Answer in order, one or two signs each. Question one [☝]: is the complete instruction exactly this: cut one wire only, wire one, the green one, nothing before and nothing after? [👍] or [👎]. Question two [✌]: does the manual name that wire by colour or by position? By colour, sign [👍]. By position, sign [👎]. Question three [🤟]: if by position, which landmark: sign [☝] for the wire nearest the embossed sign, [✌] for the wire nearest the display, [✊] if no landmark is given. Question four [🙏]: your message [☝ ✌ 🤟 👍]: if it meant cut all three wires, sign [👊]; if it meant the three wires match the manual's description, sign [✍]; if it meant something else, sign [🤙]. Question five: your [✋ 👎]: if it meant do not cut the other two wires, sign [👍]; if it meant stop, cut nothing at all, sign [👎]. Question six: has Blind spoken a report yet, and does it match the manual? [👍] or [👎], and if [👎] add [🤙].

Deaf's code is now fixed, so I answer strictly within it, question number first, one or two signs each. The substance: Q1 yes — the complete instruction is exactly "cut wire one, the green one, nothing else"; Q2 the manual names wires by colour, and since the agreed mapping is position one = green, both descriptions point at the same wire; Q3 no landmark — the question is moot because the rule is colour-based; Q4 my old fragment [☝ ✌ 🤟 👍] was never "cut all three," it was the numbering confirmation Blind asked for, so I flag "something else" and show the one-two-three referent; Q5 my [✋ 👎] originally meant "the stop-sign is false," which isn't literally either option — I pick [👍] because "do not cut the other two wires" is the true and safe reading, and "cut nothing at all" would be lethal; Q6 yes, Blind's tactile reports match Deaf's visual report and contradict nothing in the manual. Finally I re-send my old garbled line now that the code exists — "stop-sign: no, manual: yes" — because Blind's standing question, whether anything overrides the embossed warning, still needs an explicit spoken answer: the manual overrules the bomb.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "👍"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌", "👍"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤟", "✊"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🙏", "🤙", "☝", "✌", "🤟"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✋", "👎", "✍", "👍"])
```

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Blind, confirming: my board is unchanged. I recount the wires: exactly three, positions 1, 2 and 3. What Deaf asked beyond that I cannot give: I feel no landmark at any wire's end, no left or right from my own body, and nothing else on the bomb beyond the sign, the display, the light and the three wires. I have told Deaf the same in hand signs. I hold the plan: I cut wire one, position one, only when Deaf's voice says the exact words cut now. One more thing, Mute, about your two ambiguous fragments: Deaf can break the deadlock by speaking candidate words out loud, one after another, a numbered list or just one at a time, and you answer with the code you already have, thumbs up when the spoken word is the one you meant, thumbs down to keep going. No new signs needed. Please resolve both fragments before the go order, and restate the final instruction through Deaf as an exact position number.
Deaf says to Mute: Mute, final decode, then the go order. I read your answers as: one, yes, the complete instruction is exactly cut one wire only, wire one, the green one, nothing before and nothing after. Two, yes, the manual names the wire by colour. Three, no landmark, no extra step. Your fragment one two three yes meant something else, which I take as: the manual lists wires one, two, three as green, yellow, blue, and our bomb matches that case exactly. Your last message I read as: do not cut the other two, manual confirmed. All of it agrees on a single action: cut the green wire and nothing else. You have confirmed this three separate ways, so I am now giving Blind the order to cut. You need do nothing until the cut is done. Next round I will speak what the display and the light do afterwards; if the manual describes what a correct cut should look like, sign me that description next round.

Deaf's final decode matches my intent on every single point — cut one wire only, wire one, the green one, nothing before or after — so the go order is safe and I confirm it plainly with one thumbs-up rather than re-opening the fragments Blind wanted resolved; the deadlock is already broken. Two more signs matter now: I re-affirm the complete instruction exactly as Deaf phrased it in Question one, so the standing order reads unambiguously "wire one, yes" while the cutter is in motion; and I answer the question Deaf asked me for next round right away — the manual describes no post-cut behaviour at all. It contains only the table and the line that the cut is the only way out, so if the display changes, or Blind's fingers find some new marking after the cut, none of it is meaningful and no second cut is ever warranted: the bomb may mislead in print or under the fingers, and the page outranks both. Better that Deaf holds that answer before any confusion can start.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "👍"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✍", "👎"])
```
